sentences.text: The species Antineosteus rufus likely grew to over three meters long, a size inferred by comparing its plates with those of better-preserved relatives.
The genus was formally described by Lelièvre in 1984.
Its large body and absence of bladed jaw teeth suggest it fed on plankton or suspended particles, much like modern baleen whales or whale sharks.
This animal belongs to the family Homostiidae within the class Placodermi and is most closely related to the genus Homostius.
Fossils date from the Pragian to Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago, found in Morocco and the Czech Republic.
